feature: Certified initial multispan Loft fits between length stations
native_reference: Rhino 8.32.26160.13001 public Brep.CreateFromLoftRefit, Loft commands and Curve.GetDistancesBetweenCurves
observations: Multispan initial candidates can pass three interior length stations within half the requested tolerance even when the complete deviation exceeds that reserve. Such candidates now require a separate continuous complete source-to-candidate bound within the full requested tolerance. Existing half-tolerance admission remains sufficient.

The three stations are quarter, midpoint and three-quarter entries of the existing nine-entry incremental length batch at fractional stopping precision 1e-4. This is an independently implemented selection rule qualified by the cited complete native records, not a claim to have established Rhino internal adaptive sampling.

All 32 older partial-interval records and 50 new representation/style/API/command records reproduce complete native values at 1e-9. The new capture covers degree elevation, negative uniform weight gauges, translated/permuted frames, reversal and all five styles. Ordinary API source definitions remain unchanged; commands retain source presence, selection and valid output topology.

The curved multispan holdouts vary tolerance near initial-fit transitions for two curved source definitions and their unequal spatial distributions. Four of eighteen native initial fits remain conservatively rejected, along with all six native cases requiring extra pieces. Fourteen holdouts are admitted, each comparing the complete native record at 1e-9.

A direct regression has an actual initial-candidate error above half tolerance and receives a certified full-tolerance fit. Another source agrees at all three stations but has an unsampled bump above full tolerance; it is rejected without source mutation.

The 52 public deviation measurements cover six intervals, four original source clocks, both directions and four hidden-feature cases. Scalar maximum/minimum deviations are compared to SMLib; tied witness parameters are not prescribed. Native maxima are invariant across the tested clocks and reversal, so this public geometric maximum alone does not explain source-clock-dependent adaptive subdivision.

The two multispan command-history cases retain source objects and selection, create one undo step, preserve Redo after a tighter unsupported fit, and replay the same result. The original multispan history case was moved into a focused module beside the new case.

Legacy source-clock subdivision, unequal-region joining counterexamples and single-input smooth preparation remain unfinished. Existing historical measurement fields and native capture bytes are unchanged.
